transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-25
Start time: 15:00 PDT
Duration: ~42 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Shah (Redwood SE), Dan Liu (Hightide CTO), Maya Rivera (Hightide ML Eng), Sam Ortiz (Hightide Product)

00:00 Alex Moreno: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time. quick intro — I'm Alex, AE at Redwood, and Priya is our systems engineer. did everyone get the calendar invite?   
00:04 Dan Liu: Yep, thanks Alex. Dan here. we're excited to talk through model choices. we run the onboard assistant on our fleet and it's getting to the point where context size and cost matter.  
00:12 Priya Shah: Great. can you give a quick overview of current stack and main pain points?  
00:18 Dan Liu: Sure. currently we use an in-house finetuned model on GPU instances — mostly 16k context. latencies are fine for single-turn but we see big spikes when the convo history grows, and the vector DB lookups add extra hops. also need better multilingual performance — esp Japanese — and tool-calling to trigger telemetry retrieval and run domain-specific tools.  
00:38 Maya Rivera: And from ML perspective, we need consistent tokenization across languages. some open models tokenizers chop japanese awkwardly, and that hurts seq2seq paraphrasing.  
00:50 Alex Moreno: Understood. sounds like three Qs: 1) can we hit 32k→64k context reliably, 2) multilingual quality, and 3) tool/function calling workflows. is that fair?  
00:59 Sam Ortiz: Yep, and also cost — we have to compare Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. we'll likely start hosted but want to know migration path if throughput grows.  
01:07 Priya Shah: Excellent. quickly on Redwood side — our Hosted API supports streaming, function-calling, and a model catalog of verified open weights. Dedicated gives you reserved GPU pools with predictable throughput and private deployments give VPC/on-prem with KMS/HSM. there may be slight perf delta depending on infra and quant settings.  
01:28 Dan Liu: How do open models compare on long context? we saw Mistral variants kind of drop off after 32k.  
01:34 Priya Shah: Yeah, good callout. short answer: model architecture and implementation matter. Mistral-instruct-style models are strong up to 32k in our tests. for 64k we often look at Llama 3 70B derivatives or models optimized for long memory — and Redwood's runtime manages KV cache and continuous batching to keep latency within SLOs.  
01:55 Maya Rivera: Are we talking about native 64k context models or chunking and retrieval?  
01:59 Priya Shah: Both approaches exist. native 64k context models give simpler semantics but cost more memory. chunking + retrieval with smart prefix KV cache is our common pattern — you get most of the benefit at lower cost. Priya: (laughs) sorry that's my voice.  
02:12 Dan Liu: there's also the tool-calling piece — we need function calling to pull telemetry and call our safety validators in backend with low extra latency.  
02:20 Alex Moreno: Redwood supports tool-calling via function invocation schema — we've integrated with customers' HTTP webhooks and RPC layers. the main tradeoff is if you need private network calls (on-prem) vs calling out from hosted.  
02:30 Sam Ortiz: For security we need SOC 2, audit logs, and KMS for keys. VPC peering or on-prem would be ideal. what's Redwood's position?  
02:36 Priya Shah: Hosted has SOC 2 and audit logs; we offer dedicated with private networking and an enterprise private deployment option where the control plane can be customer-managed. KMS/HSM integration is supported for Private. note some customers choose dedicated for predictable latency and data isolation while keeping control plane hosted.  
02:55 Maya Rivera: On multilingual benchmarks — which open models are performing best for Japanese and Spanish?  
03:00 Priya Shah: In our evals, Mistral variants and Falcon-releases do well for Spanish. For Japanese, models with Japanese pretraining or multilingual instruction-tuning (some Llama 3 weights or proprietary open variants) tend to outperform baseline Llama 2. but it's noisy — tokenizer differences and training data coverage make big swings.  
03:21 Dan Liu: Could Redwood run a quick eval on our data? we can strip PII and share a few thousand convo snippets.  
03:27 Alex Moreno: Absolutely. that's a typical next step. Priya: can you outline the minimal artifacts we need?  
03:32 Priya Shah: Prefer anonymized prompt/response pairs, a couple of long-history threads (10–30k tokens), and a set of tool-calling examples with expected outputs. we'll also want throughput targets to size Dedicated pools if you go that route.  
03:46 Sam Ortiz: Throughput target — peak 30 reqs/sec, average 8 reqs/sec. latencies ideally <500ms p50 for short turns, p95 under 1.5s where possible.  
03:58 Priya Shah: Noted. that helps size batching and GPU selection.  
04:02 Dan Liu: On cost — what's the ballpark per-token cost difference Hosted vs Dedicated if we commit?  
04:08 Alex Moreno: quick ballpark — Hosted is higher per token but includes the control plane, monitoring, autoscaling. Dedicated with reserved capacity can be 30–60% cheaper at scale depending on utilization and quant profiles. we'll send a detailed pricing sheet.  
04:24 Maya Rivera: One technical question: how does Redwood handle KV cache invalidation when model rollouts happen? we've had cache misalignment during our A/B tests.  
04:32 Priya Shah: Good one. we version cache keys with model and rollout id — when you do canaries we keep separate caches and fall back to the previous variant for incompatible caches. sometimes ops slip-ups cause mismatch but our console shows per-route cache stats to debug.  
04:49 Dan Liu: OK. latency vs accuracy tradeoff — we might quantize some models. what's Redwood's recommendation?  
04:56 Priya Shah: Quantization usually reduces memory and cost, but depends on accuracy tolerance. we recommend 4-bit quant for many workloads, test for regen quality on your eval set. Redwood Optimize can suggest quant profiles.  
05:10 Sam Ortiz: Regarding tool-calling, we want deterministic outputs for validators. do you support strict function schemas?  
05:16 Priya Shah: Yes — function call schemas and structured output checks are supported. you can enforce JSON schema and set automatic retries/fallbacks if the model output fails validation.  
05:26 Dan Liu: Any pitfalls with private/on-prem deployments we should be aware of?  
05:30 Priya Shah: On-prem adds ops overhead — networking, GPU procurement, maintenance. our private control plane option reduces ops by centralizing some control, but air-gapped on-prem requires a bit more integration time. also model updates/patches are more manual.  
05:46 Maya Rivera: For the eval, can we also get token counts and cost estimates per model variant?  
05:51 Alex Moreno: Yes, we'll include per-token cost assumptions in the bench report. Priya will run Mistral, Falcon, Llama 3 variants, plus Redwood-verified open weights with 32k/64k settings.  
06:02 Priya Shah: Quick note — sometimes transcripts or tokens are mis-estimated for non-latin scripts; we'll double-check tokenizer token counts for Japanese.  
06:10 Dan Liu: Perfect. any usage limits or rate-limiting on Hosted we should plan for?  
06:15 Alex Moreno: Hosted has default quotas but we can provision higher throughput for pilots. Dedicated removes many rate limits since you own the pool.  
06:24 Sam Ortiz: Who should be our main contact for security docs?  
06:27 Alex Moreno: I'll send the SOC 2 and ISO summaries. Priya will share the security integration notes and our KMS guide.  
06:34 Dan Liu: timeline — we're hoping to decide vendor by mid-July; pilot in August.  
06:38 Alex Moreno: Sounds attainable. we'll prioritize the eval and pricing.  
06:42 Maya Rivera: small nit: we've seen provider names slightly mispronounced in other transcripts, so if you say 'KV cache' sometimes it's transcribed as 'KV cash' (laughs) — just flagging.  
06:52 Priya Shah: (laughs) noted.  
06:55 Alex Moreno: OK quick recap and next steps: Priya will run the 32k/64k benchmarks and tokenizer checks and share a perf matrix by 6/30; Alex will send pricing and security docs by 7/2; Hightide will upload anonymized sample prompts and throughput targets by 7/6. we'll schedule a technical deep dive to review results week of July 6. any objections?  
07:18 Dan Liu: none from me.  
07:22 Sam Ortiz: good. thanks everyone.  
07:25 Alex Moreno: thanks, bye!

End of transcript.
